title: Graceful decommission scheduler with traffic-shaping and capacity reservations
creator: Leah Park
description:
Problem statement: Performing node lifecycle operations (drain, reprovision, kernel/driver upgrades, retirement) in Dedicated fleets frequently causes transient throughput drops or elevated tail latency for affected customers. Existing maintenance flows require manual window selection and ad-hoc capacity reservations, leading to either over-provisioning or customer-visible throttling.

Goal: Build a Graceful Decommission Scheduler that autonomously proposes low-impact maintenance windows, orchestrates staged drains with traffic shaping and temporary capacity reservations, and coordinates with autoscaling policies and throughput guarantees to keep SLOs stable during maintenance. The system should provide an API and Console controls for operators to approve/snooze windows, visualize risk, and rollback a drain if throughput degrades.

Scope and deliverables:
- Offline analysis service that analyzes historical per-cluster/per-region traffic patterns (p95/p99, request volume by hour, peak shift) and generates a ranked list of candidate maintenance windows with risk scores.
- A scheduler component that creates maintenance plans: group nodes into N waves, reserve ephemeral capacity or scale up quota before drain, and apply traffic shaping weights to gradually reduce load from nodes in the current wave.
- Integration hooks with the autoscaler to pre-warm capacity and verify capacity readiness prior to draining a wave.
- Run-time verification: telemetry checks (latency, error rate, throughput) with automatic abort and rollback when thresholds exceeded.
- Console UI additions: suggested windows, risk visualization, manual override, and a timeline view of staged drains.

Non-goals: full general-purpose traffic engineering for customer apps, changes to customer routing logic, or on-host kernel upgrade automation beyond triggering existing upgrade flow.

Design trade-offs and notes: we will prefer conservative reservations (temporary burst capacity) for initial rollout to minimize customer impact; more aggressive bin-packing/overlap optimization can be explored in follow-ups. Risk of over-reserving capacity is mitigated via cost alerts and configurable reservation caps per account/region.

Primary stakeholders: Fleet Reliability, Runtime Engineering, Console UX, Dedicated Sales (enterprise customers).
acceptance_criteria: Scheduler generates at least three candidate maintenance windows per cluster with associated risk scores and expected throughput impact estimates
A maintenance plan can be created that stages node drains into multiple waves (configurable wave_size and inter_wave_delay)
Autoscaler integration exists: scheduler can request pre-warm capacity and receive readiness callback before commencing a wave
Traffic-shaping policy applied during drain reduces connection assignment to draining nodes gradually over a configurable ramp-down period
Run-time verification aborts the plan and attempts to rollback if latency or error rate breaches configured thresholds within a wave
Console surfaces suggested windows, a timeline of waves, risk score and an approval/snooze flow
End-to-end e2e test simulating a medium-sized cluster demonstrates <5% sustained throughput loss at p95 during a typical 3-wave drain under nominal load
updates: 2026-02-19: Kickoff meeting with Fleet Reliability and Runtime. Agreed to target conservative default wave sizes (10% of active capacity) and a 10-minute inter-wave verification window.

2026-02-25: Prototype of window-suggester completed. Uses 90-day rolling traffic histogram and credit-based risk scoring. Early results correlate low-traffic windows to 02:00-05:00 UTC for NA-east clusters.
2026-03-02: Design review with Console team. Decided on a minimal UI that lists top 3 suggestions and an advanced modal for custom plans. UX to include predicted cost delta for reservations.
2026-03-05: Integration spike with autoscaler (ENG-34211). Discovered race where scale-up readiness signal is delivered asynchronously; added handshake protocol requirement.

2026-03-09: Bench test on staging: 3-wave drain with pre-warm achieved rollback thresholds triggered correctly in 2/3 runs — investigation points to KV cache eviction timing; follow-up with runtime team required.
2026-03-10: Blocker identified: need a non-disruptive KV cache warmup path or soft-eviction strategy before draining heavy-traffic nodes (assigning to ENG-51780).
next_steps: Finalize autoscaler handshake spec and add readiness API (coord with ENG-34211)
Implement conservative reservation allocator and quota caps; add cost estimation to suggestion UI
Prototype traffic-shaping balancer and implement gradual ramp-down policy in staging
Add KV cache warmup/soft-eviction experiment with Runtime team and re-run bench tests
Prepare a limited rollout plan for non-SLA enterprise customers and gather metrics for two weeks
